title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: GL_2-type group schemes over a base S, as in the surrounding pages of the 'équation des lacets' notes. T_rho and T_sigma are the commutative tori (centralizers) attached to elements rho and sigma. N'_sigma is a normalizer-type extension of T_sigma, with N'_sigma/T_sigma = mu_2. Prefixes: S means det = 1; S' means (det)^2 = 1. On the previous page Grothendieck obtained direct-product decompositions (123): R_{rho,sigma} = S'T_rho x SN'_sigma x G_m and R deg_{rho,sigma} = ST_rho x ST_sigma x G_m. Here R_{rho,sigma} = Ker(Theta~: M_{rho,sigma} -> PG), as the next page states.

This page makes the canonical map R_{rho,sigma} -> T_{rho,sigma} explicit in these coordinates. T_{rho,sigma} is the subgroup {(a,b) in T_rho x N'_sigma | (det a / det b)^2 = 1}. Since T_{rho,sigma} embeds in T_rho x N'_sigma, it suffices to give the two components.

(124) The map is (a,b,lambda) |-> (lambda a, lambda b), with lambda acting as a scalar. It lands in T_{rho,sigma} because both det(lambda a)^2 and det(lambda b)^2 equal lambda^4.

Kernel: lambda a = 1 and lambda b = 1 force a = b = lambda^{-1} (a scalar).
- lambda^{-1} in S'T_rho gives lambda^{-4} = 1.
- lambda^{-1} in SN'_sigma gives lambda^{-2} = 1.
Hence lambda is in mu_2, and the kernel is the diagonal {(lambda,lambda,lambda)}, using lambda^{-1} = lambda.

(125) This diagonal mu_2 is identified with R_{rho,sigma} ∩ SG. It sits inside R deg_{rho,sigma} = ST_rho x ST_sigma x G_m, inside R_{rho,sigma}.

(126) Hence T_{rho,sigma} = (S'T_rho x SN'_sigma x G_m)/mu_2, with mu_2 embedded diagonally.

Surjectivity of (124), which the page does not state, holds fppf-locally. Given (x,y), choose lambda with lambda^2 = det y. Then b = lambda^{-1} y has det 1, and a = lambda^{-1} x satisfies (det a)^2 = (det x / det y)^2 = 1. So (126) is an fppf quotient, étale if 2 is invertible.

(127) The three canonical maps mu_2 -> ST_rho, mu_2 -> ST_sigma and mu_2 -> G_m (scalar ±1) give an embedding mu_2^3 -> R deg -> R. Its diagonal recovers (125). He remarks this is nothing other than the earlier (48).

The next page uses the decomposition to compute the centre of M_{rho,sigma}.

Purpose: an explicit structure theory of the stabilizer and centralizer group schemes that occur in a moduli or classification problem for pairs (rho, sigma) of 2x2 matrices. This feeds the study of the loop equation in the Longue Marche / Teichmüller-tower context.
errors: Minor slip in the marginal check: he writes det(lambda a)^2 = lambda^2. In fact det(lambda a) = lambda^2 det a, so det(lambda a)^2 = lambda^4 (det a)^2 = lambda^4, and likewise for b. The equality he needs still holds.
The page does not state that (124) is surjective, which (126) requires. It is true fppf-locally (extract a square root of det b); this is not étale-local unless 2 is invertible on S.
Small gap: deducing a = lambda^{-1} from lambda a = 1 implicitly uses that scalars lie in T_rho and N'_sigma. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Presentation of the group scheme T_{rho,sigma} as a quotient (S'T_rho x SN'_sigma x G_m)/mu_2 with mu_2 embedded diagonally, via scaling by a central G_m
ideas.modern_name: central isogeny / quotient by diagonal mu_2 (analogue of GL_2 = (SL_2 x G_m)/mu_2)
ideas.where_published: general techniques in SGA 3; the specific T_{rho,sigma} only in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: Identification of the kernel R_{rho,sigma} ∩ SG with the diagonal mu_2, and the embedding mu_2^3 into R deg_{rho,sigma}
ideas.modern_name: computation of centres/kernels of reductive-type subgroup schemes of GL_2

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine group-scheme bookkeeping computation (a diagonal-mu_2 quotient presentation, like GL_2 = (SL_2 x G_m)/mu_2) inside a long unpublished calculation. It is correct up to a trivial slip and contains no new idea or connection.
